3. Low wages: While factory owners made significant profits, workers received low wages that barely covered their basic needs. Workers often had to rely on their entire families working in factories to stay afloat.

4. No job security: Workers had no job security and could be dismissed at any time. This made it difficult for workers to plan for their futures or invest in their own education or skills.

5. Child labor: Children as young as six or seven years old were employed in factories, working in dangerous conditions for low pay. Child labor was widely accepted during this time and was seen as a way for families to supplement their income.
